title: Char Siu Pork
subtitle: Chinese BBQ pork belly with honey and five-spice
excerpt: Pork belly strips marinated in soy, honey and five-spice, then roasted until lacquered and caramelised at the edges. The glaze is sticky, savoury and sweet all at once. Serve over rice or in steamed buns.
sourceNotes: Char siu literally means 'fork-roasted' in Cantonese, referring to the traditional skewers used in Chinese BBQ restaurants. This oven method gets close to the same lacquered result.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cooked and cooled pork slices. Reheat in a hot oven for 8 minutes.

content.text: Line the roasting tin with foil and place a rack over it. The pork needs to sit above any drips so the heat can circulate and the glaze can set properly.
Mix the soy sauces, honey, five-spice, mirin, garlic, ginger and sesame oil in a large bowl.
Add the pork strips and turn to coat. Cover and chill for at least 2 hours.
Heat your oven to 200°C. Line a roasting tin with foil.
Lift the pork out of the marinade and place in the tin. Keep the marinade.
Roast for 15 minutes. Brush with the reserved marinade, then roast for another 15 minutes.
The pork is done when the edges are caramelised and sticky. Rest for 5 minutes before slicing.

items.symptom: Glaze burns before the pork is cooked through.
items.cause: Oven too hot or glaze applied too early.
items.fix: Cover loosely with foil and reduce oven to 180°C.

items.symptom: Pork is pale and not caramelised.
items.cause: Oven not hot enough or glaze not brushed on.
items.fix: Brush glaze on and blast under a hot grill for 3 minutes.

items.cause: Soy sauce ratio is too high.
items.fix: Add an extra tablespoon of honey to balance.
